```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

Nested resampling estimates how well a tuning procedure performs on new
data. It runs two loops. The inner loop tunes the model, and the outer loop
scores the tuned model on rows that the tuning never saw.

The best score from ordinary tuning is optimistic. The same resamples that
score the candidates also pick the winner, so part of its score is luck.
`vignette("estimate")` explains this in more detail.

```{r deps, include = FALSE}
needed <- c("tidymodels", "ranger")
missing_pkgs <- needed[
  !vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
has_deps <- length(missing_pkgs) == 0L
```

```{r deps-notice, eval = !has_deps, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(
  "This guide attaches the **tidymodels** packages and fits random forests",
  "with the **ranger** package.",
  if (length(missing_pkgs) == 1L) {
    sprintf("The **%s** package is not installed here,", missing_pkgs)
  } else {
    sprintf(
      "The **%s** packages are not installed here,",
      paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = "** and **")
    )
  },
  "so the rest of this guide has been skipped. Install",
  if (length(missing_pkgs) == 1L) "it" else "them",
  "and rebuild to see it.\n"
)

knitr::knit_exit()
```

```{r libraries, message = FALSE}
library(tidymodels)
library(nestedtune)
```

## The design

We start with the design. `nested_resamples()` builds an outer resampling
and attaches an inner resampling to each outer fold.

```{r design}
set.seed(1)

folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = vfold_cv(v = 5),
  inside = vfold_cv(v = 5)
)

folds
```

Each row is one outer fold. `splits` holds the outer split.
`inner_resamples` holds an ordinary rset built from that fold's analysis
set alone, so the tuning in that fold never sees the fold's held-out rows.

```{r inner}
folds$inner_resamples[[1]]
```

`mtcars` has `r nrow(mtcars)` rows, which keeps this example fast.

## The model and the grid

We tune two parameters of a random forest over a grid of candidates, the
settings to try.

```{r workflow}
rf <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger") |>
  set_mode("regression")

wf <- workflow(mpg ~ ., rf)

grid <- expand.grid(mtry = c(2L, 5L, 8L), min_n = c(2L, 10L))
grid
```

The grid has `r nrow(grid)` candidates. Each of the `r nrow(folds)` outer
folds scores all of them on `r nrow(folds$inner_resamples[[1]])` inner
resamples. That is
`r nrow(folds) * nrow(folds$inner_resamples[[1]]) * nrow(grid)` fits for
tuning, plus one fit per outer fold for scoring.

## Running the loop

`nested_tune_grid()` runs the outer loop. For each outer fold, it calls
`tune::tune_grid()` on the fold's inner resamples and picks the best
candidate. It then fits that candidate on the fold's analysis set and
scores it on the assessment set.

We pass no metric set, so the run uses tune's default for regression and
selects by `rmse`. To select another way, pass a `selection_rule()` as
`select`. We call `set.seed()` first, as elsewhere in tidymodels. The same
seed gives the same result whether the folds run serially or in parallel.

```{r run}
set.seed(2)

res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = grid)

res
```

`summary()` describes the run in words.

```{r summarize}
summary(res)
```

## The number to report

```{r estimate}
est <- collect_metrics(res)
est

rmse_row <- filter(est, .metric == "rmse")
```

The RMSE of `r round(rmse_row$mean, 2)` is the mean of `r rmse_row$n`
outer scores. Each one was measured on rows that the tuning never saw.
`std_err` is the standard error of that mean.

This estimate describes the whole procedure (tune, select, fit) and not one
fitted model. It is still the number to report for the model that
`nested_final_fit()` fits below, because that model comes from the same
procedure.

## Each fold's selection

Each outer fold tunes on its own, so the folds can choose different
settings. `collect_selections()` lists what each fold chose.

```{r selected}
selected <- collect_selections(res)

selected
```

```{r instability}
n_mtry <- n_distinct(selected$mtry)
n_min_n <- n_distinct(selected$min_n)
```

Across `r nrow(res)` outer folds, `mtry` took `r n_mtry` distinct values
and `min_n` took `r n_min_n`. When the folds disagree on a parameter, its
value is largely arbitrary at this sample size.

`autoplot()` draws the selections, one point per outer fold. A flat row
means that the folds agreed.

```{r autoplot-parameters, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "One panel per tuned parameter, with one point per outer fold at the value that fold's inner tuning selected."}
autoplot(res)
```

The per-fold scores show how much the folds differ.

```{r per-fold}
per_fold <- collect_metrics(res, summarize = FALSE)
per_fold

fold_rmse <- per_fold |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  pull(.estimate)

c(sd = sd(fold_rmse), std_err = sd(fold_rmse) / sqrt(length(fold_rmse)))
```

The first number is the spread of the folds. The second is the `std_err`
that `collect_metrics()` reports, which is the precision of their mean.
Quoting the second as the spread understates how much the folds disagree.

The other `autoplot()` view draws the per-fold scores, with a dashed line
at the nested estimate.

```{r autoplot-performance, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "One panel per metric, with one point per outer fold's score and a dashed line at the mean across folds."}
autoplot(res, type = "performance")
```

## The model to deploy

Now we build the model to deploy. `nested_final_fit()` runs the same
procedure once more on all the data. It takes the inner resampling, grid,
metrics and selection rule from `res`, so the model and the estimate come
from one search.

```{r final}
set.seed(3)

final <- nested_final_fit(wf, res)

final
```

The outer folds play no part here. The object predicts directly.

```{r predict}
predict(final, new_data = mtcars[1:3, ])
```

`extract_tune_results()` returns the tuning run behind this model, and
`show_best()` gives its best score.

```{r comparison}
best_selection <- extract_tune_results(final) |>
  show_best(metric = "rmse", n = 1)

tibble(
  quantity = c("nested estimate (report this)", "best selection-time score"),
  rmse = c(rmse_row$mean, best_selection$mean)
)
```

The best selection-time score is not an estimate of performance on new
data, because the same resamples chose the model. Whether it lands above or
below the nested estimate here means nothing.

## The write-up

Here is a short report of this run.

> Hyperparameters (`mtry`, `min_n`) were tuned over a
> `r nrow(grid)`-point grid by `r nrow(folds$inner_resamples[[1]])`-fold
> cross-validation, nested inside a `r nrow(folds)`-fold outer
> cross-validation (n = `r nrow(mtcars)`). The outer folds give an
> estimated RMSE of `r format(round(rmse_row$mean, 2), nsmall = 2)`
> (SE `r format(round(rmse_row$std_err, 2), nsmall = 2)`) for the tuning
> procedure. The folds selected `r n_mtry` distinct values of `mtry` and
> `r n_min_n` of `min_n`. The deployed model applies the same procedure to
> the full dataset, which selected mtry = `r final$selected$mtry` and
> min_n = `r final$selected$min_n`.
